content: Do not take lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as it may harm the fetus. The combination of lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide is prescribed to treat high blood pressure. Lisinopril belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, which work by reducing certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, or water pill, that helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt through urine. This medication is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide manage high blood pressure but do not cure it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, or any other medications, including ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril, captopril, enalapril) or sulfa drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Mention specific drugs such as NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), barbiturates, cholestyramine, colestipol, digoxin, insulin, oral diabetes medications, lithium, steroids, other diuretics, blood pressure medications, pain relievers, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are on dialysis, undergoing desensitization therapy, or have a history of allergies, asthma, diabetes, gout, high cholesterol, collagen vascular diseases (e.g., lupus, scleroderma), heart failure, reduced urination, stroke, heart, kidney, or liver disease, or angioedema (a condition causing swelling and difficulty breathing or swallowing). Notify your doctor if you plan to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are having surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol, as it may worsen side effects. Be aware that diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, or excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing dizziness or fainting. Lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide may also cause dizziness or fainting when standing up too quickly, especially when starting the medication. To prevent this, rise slowly from a lying position and rest your feet on the floor before standing. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If prescribed a low-salt or low-sodium diet or an exercise program, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide may cause side effects. Common side effects include dizziness, headache, cough, fatigue, tingling in the hands or feet, decreased sexual ability, and heartburn. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; stomach pain; nausea; vomiting; fever; sore throat; chills; muscle pain or weakness; yellowing of the skin or eyes; dry mouth; thirst; confusion; seizures; reduced urination; chest pain; irregular heartbeat; pain in the big toe; tingling in the limbs; loss of muscle tone; leg heaviness; fatigue; or cold, gray skin. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness, fainting, blurred vision, dry mouth, thirst, weakness, drowsiness, restlessness, confusion, seizures, muscle pain or cramps, infrequent urination, nausea, vomiting, or rapid or irregular heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Regular blood pressure checks and lab tests may be necessary to monitor your response to the medication. Inform your doctor and lab personnel that you are taking lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide before any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist with any questions about refills.
